title: 2x Tradescantia chrysophylla ‘Baby Bunny Bellies’ - Mini Houseplant plug - Hardy
description:
Description:
 

  Tradescantia chrysophylla ‘Baby Bunny Bellies’
 
 is a low-growing, evergreen trailing perennial, popular for its soft, velvety foliage. The pointed, oval leaves are dark grey-green on top and deep purple-red underneath, giving a subtle two-tone effect. Both leaves and stems are covered with fine hairs, giving a distinctive, tactile texture reminiscent of a rabbit’s fur – this unique trait inspired its cultivar name. Although small white flowers may appear throughout the year, they are uncommon on indoor plants.


  Growing Conditions:
 

   Temperature:
  
  Tender perennial, best grown indoors in the UK or under glass. Approximate hardiness rating:
  
   H1B
  
  (minimum 10–15°C).
 

   Light:
  
  Prefers bright, filtered light or partial shade. Avoid direct sunlight, which can scorch the leaves.
 

   Soil:
  
  Use a fertile, free-draining potting mix such as peat-free houseplant or multipurpose compost.
 

   Watering:
  
  Water moderately when in active growth (spring–summer), allowing the top of the compost to dry slightly between waterings. Reduce watering in winter.
 

   Feeding:
  
  Apply a balanced houseplant feed every 3–4 weeks during the growing season.
 

   Maintenance:
  
  Easy to grow and maintain. Remove faded stems to keep growth compact. Can be pruned or pinched back to encourage bushiness. Readily propagated from stem cuttings or by division.
 

  Plant Details:
 

   Mature height:
  
  10–50 cm
 

   Spread:
  
  10–50 cm
 

   Growth habit:
  
  Clump-forming and trailing; stems root readily at nodes.
 

   Foliage:
  
  Hairy, dark green with purple-red undersides.
 

   Flowers:
  
  Small (1–1.5 cm across), white with faint pink tones, occasionally appearing year-round.
 

   Position:
  
  Part shade to bright, indirect light.
 

   Exposure:
  
  Best in a sheltered indoor position such as a conservatory, windowsill, or plant shelf.
 

  Background:
 

 This cultivar is accepted under the name
 
  Tradescantia chrysophylla ‘Baby Bunny Bellies’
 
 and was first listed online in 2008, later confirmed in print in 2025. Formerly known in cultivation under the informal name
 
  “Speedy Jenny”
 
 , it has since been standardised and recognised for its unique combination of dense, soft hairs and trailing habit. Belonging to the family Commelinaceae, the plant species
 
  Tradescantia chrysophylla
 
 was scientifically described in 2017 after its use in horticulture had already become widespread.


  Issues:
 

 Relatively pest-free, though occasionally susceptible to red spider mite, mealybugs, vine weevil, aphids, or thrips. Excess water may cause root or stem rot. The plant’s sap may cause skin irritation; handle with gloves if sensitive.


  Uses:
 

 An ideal trailing houseplant for windowsills, shelves, or hanging baskets. Adds colour, soft texture, and contrast among foliage plants. Can also be used outdoors in containers during warm summer months, but must be returned indoors before temperatures drop.


  Key Features for eBay Listing:
 

  Distinctive velvety foliage with green and purple tones
 

  Fast-growing, trailing plant – perfect for hanging planters or shelves
 

  Easy-care indoor species with soft, tactile leaves
